generalfeedback: Below is the formula for integration by parts. calc_int_methods_parts From the product rule for differentiating \(u\left(x\right)v\left(x\right)\) we can derive the rule for integration by parts, namely: \[\int u\left(x\right)v'\left(x\right)\, dx= u\left(x\right)v\left(x\right)- \int u'\left(x\right)v\left(x\right)\, dx.\] We set \(u\left(x\right)={{CT:1}}\) and \(v'\left(x\right)={{CT:2}}\), so \(u'\left(x\right)={{CT:3}}\) and \(v\left(x\right)={{CT:4}}\). Then \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:0}}\,dx&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}}-\int {{CT:6}} \,dx,\\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}}-\frac{{CT:7}}{{CT:8}}+c. \end{array}\] Where \(c\) is an integral constant.

on_true.feedback:
You appear to have used the formula \[\int u\left(x\right)v'\left(x\right)\, dx= u\left(x\right)v\left(x\right)+ \int u'\left(x\right)v\left(x\right)\, dx,\]

which is not the correct formula for integration by parts.
